subject.title: [Feature]: deterministic context injection for bootstrap files and session-type filtering

question: Should OpenClaw add dynamic command expansion to high-authority bootstrap files, or limit this issue to declarative session-scoped bootstrap selection plus the existing session_status time path?
rationale: The remaining work changes public config semantics and may execute commands while assembling system context, which is a product and security boundary that source inspection cannot choose safely.

options.title: Narrow declarative policy
options.body: Add a documented session-scoped bootstrap selector with tests and keep command execution out of bootstrap files unless a separate security design approves it.

options.title: Full dynamic bootstrap
options.body: Allow bootstrap command expansion too, but require a trust model, permissions, auditability, and cache-stability story before implementation.

options.title: Plugin/hook-only direction
options.body: Keep core behavior minimal and ask users to solve dynamic or custom bootstrap selection through reviewed hooks/plugins instead of new agents.defaults config.

recommendation.title: Narrow declarative policy
recommendation.body: Add a documented session-scoped bootstrap selector with tests and keep command execution out of bootstrap files unless a separate security design approves it.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a cross-cutting core prompt/config/security direction choice, and steipete is the best available routing candidate from the inspected history.
